newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIAN TELECOM MAY BE LISTED OVERSEAS '98.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIAN TELECOM MAY BE LISTED OVERSEAS '98.

text.p: Estonia's state-owned telecommunications holding company, Estonian Telecom, could be partly listed in London or Stockholm next year, Estonia's Privatisation Agency said on Thursday.

The agency's director general Vaino Sarnet said no set arrangement was yet decided for how to privatise the company but one of the favoured suggestions was to float around 25 percent of the company overseas and 24 percent in Tallinn.
"Estonian Telecom is an interesting company with a big growth potential," Sarnet told Reuters in an interview.
"We think that floating it in London or Stockholm ... will advertise the country and could be used indirectly as a way to evaluate the country risk.
"Also international floats usually get a higher price. The capital market in Estonia is not deep enough for the coming years and as a result could undervalue the price ot Estonian Telecom."
Sarnet said the agency has estimated the value of the company but did not want to release the figures.

Estonian Telecom holds 51 percent of the fixed network operator Estonian Telephone Co Ltd, and 51 percent of Estonian Mobile Telephone Co Ltd with Swedish operator Telia and Telecom Finland each holding 24.5 percent in each comyany.
Estonian Telecom also owns 60 percent of Estonian Paging Ltd and 48 percent of Tele Media Estonia Ltd.
Sarnet said the privatisation process for Estonian Telecom needed government and parliament approval before proceeding.
"We hope to start the public offering next year and see this as realistic as long as there not too many delays through parliament or the government," he said.
He said there had already been some interest from overseas received by the agency.
"All we can say is that no firm decision has yet been made," he said.
"But we hope a final decision (on the process) will be made this year."
The privatisation of Estonian Telecom is part of the state's privatisation programme for infrastructure companies.
Estonia is nearing the end of privatising its industrial companies and holdings with a total of 1,241 privatised auction objects since regaining independence in 1991.
The agency said there was still 50 acution objects on the privatisation list.
The list of infrastructure companies to be sold includes Estonian Railways, Estonian Oil Shale Mining Co, Tallinn Port, and Estonian Energy.
